citationText: The Digital Dilemma 2, The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences: Hollywood, CA, 2012. [Online]. Available: https://www.oscars.org/science-technology/sci-tech-projects/digital-dilemma-2The growth rate of digital tape is much less than that of hard disk drives if we include external HDDs, local network storage, and most of the cloud storage. Hard disk drives, either in local storage systems and devices or through network and remote storage, appear to be undergoing a significant growth spurt. Note, though, that there are Linear Tape Open (LTO) tape-based cloud archives now available on the market, so actual cloud archive storage will likely be split between tape and HDDs. It is also clear from the survey that there is a segment of this market that will continue to rely on optical media for digital archives. Other Archiving Trends Some other observations from the archive and preservation section of the survey are shown in Table 14. Figure 9 shows the survey trends for archiving on private or public clouds. The year 2018 may indicate significant growth in the use of clouds for archiving. Conclusion M&E workflows have many different storage requirements. Content capture, post-production, content delivery, and archiving have different needs for latency, data rates, and storage capacity. Furthermore, the best combination of performance and cost can often be attained by a combination of various storage technologies in a storage system. The survey of M&E professionals’ use of various storage technologies over a nine-year period shows how these storage requirements have changed for these different applications.
